hook_text: In January 1879, a Zulu army inflicted one of the worst defeats in British colonial history. So why did the Zulu lose the war?
clip_script: Diamonds change everything. Britain now wants all of southern Africa under its control. Independent African kingdoms stand in the way. 1878: the Xhosa are defeated in the Ninth Frontier War. December 1878: Sir Bartle Frere tells the Zulu king Cetshwayo to disband his army in thirty days. Impossible. January 1879: invasion. At Isandlwana, twenty thousand Zulu warriors destroy a British camp. About one thousand three hundred die on the British side. But Britain sends thousands more soldiers, rifles and artillery. July 1879: Ulundi. The royal homestead burns. Then, at the end of 1879, the Pedi under Sekhukhune fall to British and Swazi forces. Three kingdoms in three years. Land is lost, taxes follow, and more men are pushed onto the mines.
visual_style: A whiteboard map of southern Africa with three kingdoms shaded, a diamond icon in the middle, arrows of invasion, the horns of the bull formation drawn at Isandlwana, and a square formation at Ulundi.
pacing: Fast build to Isandlwana, a pause, then a steady close.
